{{Aggro|-1|-1}} | affiliation = | race = Human | creature = Humanoid | gender = Male | location = [[Hawk's Vigil]], [[Wetlands]] | status = Killable }} '''Harlus Ashbuckle''', real name '''Martin Corinth''', is a human magus in a tent in [[Hawk's Vigil]] hailing from [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] that fled to [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]] during the [[Third War]]. After his execution was delayed and he was released from the [[Stockades]] at the behest of [[Duke Ramon III]], a member of the [[House of Nobles]], he left for the [[Wetlands]]. There he stayed for a time at the [[Deepwater Tavern]] in [[Menethil Harbor]] before moving on to the town of [[Hawk's Vigil]], where he came under suspicion of committing murder with foul magic. ==Quotes== ;Gossip What do you want? ==Objective of== * {{questlong|Alliance|24+|The Hawk's Vigil}} ==Patch changes== * {{Patch|1.16.0|note=Added.}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ashbuckle, Harlus}} [[Category:Human characters]] [[Category:Wetlands NPCs]] [[Category:Wetlands mobs]]

'''Halduron Brightwing''' is the current Ranger-General of the [[Silvermoon Remnant]], having succeeded [[Damilara Sunsorrow]]. The foremost hunter among the remaining Quel'dorei, Halduron leads the forces stationed at [[Last Runestone|the Last Runestone]] holding back the undead trying to penetrate the [[Thalassian Highlands]] through [[Scourged Pass|the Scourged Pass]].

==Quests==
* {{questlong|Alliance|10|Taming the Beast (high elf 4)|Taming the Beast|class=hunter|race=HighElf}} {{questfinish}}

==Quotes==
Once, in the echoes of time that now feels like a distant fantasy, I dreamed of donning the mantle of Ranger-General. A vision painted with the vibrant hues of ambition danced before my eyes. Yet, the years have woven a different tapestry, one marked by the harsh brushstrokes of reality.

The coveted title, once a beacon of achievement, has transformed into a weighty burden resting heavily upon these weathered shoulders of mine.

The Bloodsail Pirates have a penchant for illicit after-hours activities, especially those involving mass combat and treasure. To see that his crew has its nightly fill of extracurricular entertainment, a lone pirate captain will drop a chest in the center of Gurubashi Arena starting at midnight, and again every three hours so at '''3 AM, 6 AM, 9 AM, 12 PM, 3 PM, 6 PM, 9 PM''' and back to midnight the chest drops. The Gurubashi Arena is a free-for-all PvP area located in Stranglethorn Vale just north of Booty Bay. ==Rewards== Within [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?object=179697 Arena Treasure Chest] adventurers can frequently find Superior Healing Potions, Greater Healing Potions, Greater Mana Potion and Mana Potions. Rare as well as uncommon equipment can also be found inside the chest. Some notable equipment exclusive to the treasure chest are: {| class="fandom-table" !Item !Quality !Type |- |[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18711 Arena Bands] |Rare |Mail Wrist |- |[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18710 Arena Bracers] |Rare |Leather Wrist |- |[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18712 Arena Vambraces] |Rare |Plate Wrist |- |[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18709 Arena Wristguards] |Rare |Cloth Wrist |- |[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18706 Arena Master] |Uncommon |Trinket |} In addition, through the quests [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=7810 Arena Master] and [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=7838 Arena Grand Master], the rare trinket [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=19024 Arena Grand Master] can be obtained. Adventurers must hand in 12 [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18706 Arena Masters] to [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=14508 Short John Mithril] inside the arena to obtain the rare trinket. Note that the [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=19024 Arena Grand Master] rare trinket has no level requirements, and therefore makes for an excellent twink item. Both the [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=19024 Arena Grand Master] and the [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18706 Arena Master], however, are bind on pickup.

{{Npcbox | name = Gul'dan | image = Gul'dan.png | faction = Neutral | gender = Male | race = Orc | affiliation = Independent, [[Stormreaver clan]] | faffiliation = [[Orcish Horde]], [[Shadow Council]], [[Shadowmoon clan]] | occupation = Chieftain of the Stormreaver clan,
Master of the Shadow Council | titles = Destroyer of Dreams,''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Gul'dan Legends of the Land]'', Gul'dan
Great Betrayer''Lord of the Clans'' | status = Deceased | mentors = [[Ner'zhul]], [[Kil'jaeden]] | students = [[Cho'gall]] }} :''"I am Gul'dan... I am darkness incarnate. I will not be denied."'' :: — [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#The_History_of_Orcish_Ascension The History of Orcish Ascension] '''Gul'dan''' was the first [[orc]]ish warlock as well as the de facto founder of the [[Old Horde|Horde]]. He betrayed both his people and his mentor [[Ner'zhul]] to the demon lord [[Kil'jaeden]] for personal gain and power, and was directly responsible for the orcs' fall to demonic enslavement and their [[First War|subsequent invasion]] of Azeroth. ==Background== ===Kil'jaeden's Scheme=== Gul'dan was an apprentice to the elder shaman [[Ner'zhul]] of the [[Shadowmoon clan]]. At some point near the end of his studies with Ner'zhul, Gul'dan discovered that the shaman had been secretly trafficking with the demon lord [[Kil'jaeden]]. When push came to shove, however, Ner'zhul had been unwilling to fully embrace demonic magic, believing in the inherent nobility of the orcish people. Gul'dan, however, had no such scruples. Kil'jaeden approached Gul'dan and offered him the chance to become a master of warlock magic, on the condition that he help bring the orcs under his banner. Gul'dan accepted with no qualms whatsoever, and immediately began the work of reshaping the Orcs, hitherto a collection of simple shamanistic clans, into an unstoppable and bloodthirsty Horde.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Kil%27jaeden_and_the_Shadow_Pact Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Pact] As a necessity of his bid for power, Gul'dan trained a number of like-minded and powerful orcs, whom he named the [[Shadow Council]]. The Council was soon using its power and influence to direct almost every aspect of orcish society, so as to distract those few opposed his dark ideals from their true masters, Gul'dan and Kil'jaeden. To seal the bargain between him and Kil'jaeden, Gul'dan and the Shadow Council offered the clan chieftains the Blood of Mannoroth. The resulting Horde was bloodthirsty, barbaric, and evil, an extension of the demons whom they now worshipped.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Rise_of_the_Horde_(History_of_Warcraft) Rise of the Horde] ===The First War=== Eventually, Gul'dan was contacted by the mad sorcerer [[Medivh]] - possessed by the Dark Titan [[Sargeras]] - who offered him the promise of godhood, locked away within the [[Tomb of Sargeras]] if he would use the Horde to conquer Azeroth. Gul'dan agreed, and with the assistance of the Shadow Council, he helped Medivh open the Dark Portal between [[Azeroth]] and [[Draenor]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dark_Portal_and_the_Fall_of_Stormwind The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind] Over the next few years, Gul'dan and his Ogre-Mage apprentice [[Cho'gall]] would secretly manipulate the Horde as it rampaged across Azeroth. Gul'dan personally selected the Horde's new warchief, [[Blackhand]], as the perfect pawn for the Shadow Council after the first failed assault on Stormwind Keep by the [[Bleeding Hollow clan]] and the [[Twilight's Hammer clan]] threatened to tear the Horde apart. Though Blackhand was competent in battle and a relatively sound tactician, he was extremely lustful - and thus easy for Gul'dan to control. Gul'dan saw the Horde led to supremacy over most of the [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Kingdom of Azeroth]], but on the eve of the final siege of Stormwind, Gul'dan was aware of a raiding party against Medivh's tower of Karazhan. Realizing that the Azerothiens intended to slay the Guardian, Gul'dan hastily ransacked Medivh's mind for the Tomb's location. He was still deep within the Guardian's thoughts when [[Anduin Lothar]] and [[Khadgar]] killed him, ending Medivh's treachery and forcing Gul'dan into a coma. Without the counsel of Gul'dan, Blackhand was easily slain by [[Orgrim Doomhammer]], who, with information acquired from [[Garona]], proceeded to slaughter Gul'dan's warlocks and the majority of the Shadow Council.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#The_First_War_of_Orcish_Ascension The History of Orcish Ascension]'', The First War of Orcish Ascension ===The Second War=== Gul'dan awoke from the coma with only Cho'gall, the Twilight's Hammer, and his necrolytes still loyal to him; Blackhand, the Shadow Council and the warlocks were dead, and Garona and the other clans had betrayed him. Garona's betrayal of course had been forced. Doomhammer was willing to spare Gul'dan's life, despite his gut feeling he would one day regret this, and even let him run Balor and the ruins of Stormwind Castle, in exchange for information in regards to Blackhand's followers. This was simple enough; [[Rend Blackhand|Rend]] and [[Maim Blackhand|Maim]] hadn't professed continued loyalty to Gul'dan, so the warlock had no qualms about betraying them. Gul'dan informed Doomhammer that the raiders were preparing to join the sons of Blackhand and revolt against him, as Blackhand had once been a raider himself. Although Gul'dan's claim was untrue, Doomhammer was already suspicious of Rend and Maim and so disbanded the multitude of Wolfriders, placing them among the many grunt regiments. As a token of his "loyalty" to the Warchief, Gul'dan slaughtered his necrolytes and used their powers - combined with the spirits of the Shadow Council, the corpses of the Knights of Azeroth and their steeds - to create an army of undead - the dreaded death knights. However, Doomhammer did not suspect that they were loyal to Gul'dan alone. Before the true start of the Second War, Gul'dan founded and created his own clan, the [[Stormreaver clan|Stormreavers]], to protect him from Orgrim.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Stormreaver_Clan Clans of the Horde]'', Stormreaver Clan He also created during the ensuing conflict many ogre magi out of a band of extremely loyal ogre enforcers by warping and twisting the energy of the high elven runestones.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Ground_Units_of_the_Orcish_Horde Ground Units of the Orcish Horde]'', Ogre-Mage Secretly, Gul'dan was also amassing a great navy for the next step of his plan.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#A_Brief_History_of_the_Fall_of_Azeroth A Brief History of the Fall of Azeroth] ===Betrayal and death=== Ultimately, Gul'dan's thirst for power proved to be the Horde's undoing. On the eve of Doomhammer's attack on Lordaeron's capital, Gul'dan took the Stormreaver and Twilight's Hammer clans and set out to sea to locate the Tomb of Sargeras. With half of his standing forces suddenly gone, Doomhammer was forced to retreat and hunt down the traitorous warlock.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Tomb_of_Sargeras_(WC2_Orc) The Tomb of Sargeras (WC2 Orc)][https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Gul'dan_and_the_Betrayal Gul'dan and the Betrayal] This reprieve would ultimately give the Alliance time to regroup and retaliate. Gul'dan did indeed locate the Tomb, and used his power to raise it from the ocean floor. Taking with him his most select followers, Gul'dan cast open the doors and entered. He did not however find the godhood he was hoping for. Instead, he was torn to shreds by a swarm of insane demons that they had unleashed when the tomb was opened. The remainder of his clans, including Cho'gall and his Twilight's Hammer, were slaughtered by Doomhammer's retaliation. ===Legacy=== After Gul'dan died, his skull was turned into a channeling totem for demonic energy. The skull, at one point claimed by the [[Bonechewer clan]] as a trophy,[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Skull_of_Gul%27dan_(WC2_Orc) The Skull of Gul'dan (WC2 Orc)] was used by [[Ner'zhul]] to open portals to other worlds on Draenor, and later by Khadgar to destroy the [[Dark Portal]]. After the destruction of the Dark Portal, the skull would reappear again years later on Azeroth, this time used by the [[Burning Legion]] to corrupt the forests of [[Felwood]]. After learning of its existence from [[Arthas Menethil|Arthas]] the death knight, [[Illidan Stormrage]] found and took the skull from the dreadlord [[Tichondrius]], absorbing its power, remaining only half night elf and becoming half-demon.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/A_Destiny_of_Flame_and_Sorrow_(WC3_NightElf) A Destiny of Flame and Sorrow (WC3 NightElf)] Gul'dan's memories survived within the warlock magic of his skull and the runes he painted on the walls of the Tomb. Illidan found the Tomb using Gul'dan's memories from the Skull, and [[Maiev Shadowsong]] found the runes. A magical artifact carried by Gul'dan, the Shadow Orb, was shattered and found by Maiev. When the tomb caved in, Gul'dan's final testament was buried. His surviving loyalists in the Twilight's Hammer clan would later turn from the Burning Legion and begin worship of [[Old Gods|new masters]]. ==References== {{reflist}} {{Succession|Position created|'''[[Stormreaver clan|Chieftain of the Stormreaver clan]]'''|[[Chieftain Stormsong]]}} {{Succession|Position created|'''[[Shadow Council|Master of the Inner Circle of the Shadow Council]]'''|Unknown}} [[Category:Orc characters]] [[Category:Warlock characters]] [[Category:Deceased characters]] [[Category:Shadowmoon clan]] [[Category:Stormreaver clan]] [[Category:Shadow Council]]

HCDeaths displays and logs hardcore character deaths. It provides visual notifications (toasts), logs death details. == Installation == '''GitAddonsManager''' The easiest way to keep '''HCDeaths''' up to date is by using [[GitAddonsManager]]. # '''Add the Repository:''' Add the following URL to GitAddonsManager: https://github.com/neimad-mp/HCDeaths.git # '''Select the Branch:''' Ensure that the master branch is selected. # '''Update:''' Using GitAddonsManager, you can check for and install updates for all your AddOns with a single click. '''Manual Installation''' If you prefer manual installation, follow these steps: # Go to the main page of the repository. # Click the '''<> Code''' dropdown and download the repository as a .zip. # Unpack the .zip and rename the folder to HCDeaths, removing the -main suffix. # Move the folder into your Interface/AddOns directory and restart the game. == Git Links == * '''[https://github.com/neimad-mp/HCDeaths (neimad)]''' == Commands == {| class="fandom-table" !Command !Description |- |/hcd message |Toggle system death messages |- |/hcd move |Enable moving toast window |- |/hcd log |Toggle death log window |- |/hcd log scale [num] |Set death log scale |- |/hcd toast |Toggle toast notifications |- |/hcd toast scale [num] |Set toast popup size |- |/hcd toast time [sec] |Set toast display duration |- |/hcd progress |Toggle level progress toasts |- |/hcd color |Toggle ring colors for toast |- |/hcd deathsound |Toggle death sound on toast |- |/hcd levelsound |Toggle level-up sound on toast |- |/hcd reset |Reset all settings to defaults |} == Usage == * '''Moving Toast & Log Windows:''' Hold Ctrl + Shift and drag to reposition. Hold Ctrl + Shift and right-click to reset position. * '''Death Notifications (Toasts):''' Popups display death info with character class, level, zone, and killer details. Toasts can be scaled and timed via commands. * '''Death Logging:''' Records are stored automatically; viewable in the log window or in the saved variables file. * '''Customization:''' Toggle features such as colors, sounds, and toast progress notifications to suit your preferences. == Preview == Death List: [[File:HCD.png|frameless|200x200px]] == Death Logs == Death records are saved in: * \WTF\Account\YOUR_ACCOUNT\SavedVariables\HCDeaths.lua Example entry: [1] = { ["zone"] = "Elwynn Forest", ["stime"] = "01:41:46", ["killerName"] = "Natural Causes", ["killerClass"] = "ENV", ["killerLevel"] = "nil", ["lastWords"] = "nil", ["playerClass"] = "Rogue", ["playerLevel"] = 10, ["sdate"] = "2023/11/06", ["hcType"] = "HC", ["playerName"] = "Tents", ["deathType"] = "PVE", } [[Category:Addon]]

Harpies resemble a cross between a [[Night Elf]] female and a hunting bird, with long talons for feet, and large graceful wings for arms.  Harpies originaly hail from the [[Stonetalon Mountains]], but have since spread out across [[Kalimdor]].  Harpy legends claim that they are descend from a group of female Night Elves who were cursed by [[Queen Azshara]]. No male harpies exist, so harpies will often capture a male of another species to fill the role for a time, after which they become food for the nest. In lean times, harpies can lay unfertilized eggs that become female copies of the mother.

Vicious and predatory by nature, harpies are the bane of all other life in the areas were they take root.  They have been raiding [[Tauren]] settlements since time out of mind, and it can only be assumed that they are as much a plague on the [[Quillboar]]s and others.  The only race rumored to have any peaceful relationship with the harpies are [[Kobolds]], who trade them scavanged tools and weapons for information and protection.

If not driven out, they quickly range out attacking anything and everything they can get.  Harpies are clearly very intelligent, since they are able to communicate with other races when they wish to.  The common echelons of Harpy society attack with crude weapons or simply with their razor sharp talons. They are well used to the ways of divine magic and treachery. The more elite Harpies tend to be master of elemental storm magic and are much more dangerous.

These vile, unscrupulous winged women live only to cause mischief and sorrow.
Hailing from the windy Stonetalon Mountains, the harpies are masterful
at ambushing hapless caravans and foolish travelers alike.

Harpies are found in [[Teldrassil]], [[Stonetalon Mountains|The Stonetalon Mountains]], [[Feralas]], [[Mulgore]], [[Thousand Needles]], [[Alterac Valley]], [[Barrens|Tthe Barrens]], and [[Durotar]].


=Matriarchies=

===Witchwing===
Residing in the northern Barrens in an area called [[The Dry Hills]] this group of harpies have been ravaging the [[Horde]]'s caravan supplies. The lower sections of their group are led by so called lieutenants, called Slayers. They stand out from the rest by wearing rings. They, in turn, answer to the leader of the matriarchy [[Serena Bloodfeather]]. She is the sister of a harpy named [[Bloodfeather]] who was slain by [[Rexxar]] and her attacks on the Horde are inspired by a sense of revenge. It seems she is assisted in her leadership by [[Sister Rathtalon]]. Their plumage is black.

===Bloodfury===
In the [[Stonetalon Mountains]], the [[Tauren]] are having their own problems with the harpies. The Bloodfuries are the source of the increasing number of harpies in [[Kalimdor]]; they encroach upon all likes of life preventing the innocent from leaving their boundaries. Their leader, [[Bloodfury Ripper]], is all but a queen to the Bloodfuries. She makes her home in [[The Charred Vale]], close to [[Desolace]] where she is busy keeping out the [[Tauren]] and [[Night Elves]] who are trying to regrow the forests. Their plumage is red and white.

===Bloodfeather===
In [[Teldrassil]], the harpies have sought to nest on the night elves' own homeland. Recently grown, the great tree is a perfect location for the Bloodfeather matriarchy, who have already started laying eggs to increase the size of their tribe. The night elves are struggling to keep the number of harpies down, and give out bounties for Bloodfeather belts collected from dead harpies.

===Dustwind===
Dustwind harpies have settled down in the dry gulches and ravines of [[Durotar]], much to the annoyance of the recently settled [[orc]]s. The harpies assault caravans on the road south of [[Orgrimmar]], and have laid claim to a relatively large pocket of passages in the jagged rises just north of [[Razor Hill]]. They have blue and red plumage.

===Windfury===
The harpies of the Windfury matriarcy inhabit the new home of their ancestral enemies, the [[tauren]]. They have nests both in the southern and the northern parts of the great grasslands, and constantly harass travelers journeying to and from [[Thunder Bluff]], situated on the nearby mesa. Their plumage is blue and white.

===Northspring===
More harpies nest in the lush tropical forest of [[Feralas]]. The Northspring harpies are among the most dangerous of the matriarchies, and can quickly slaughter the unwary traveler lost in the wilds. As with most of their habitats, the harpies in Feralas clash with the local tauren tribe, base in [[Camp Mojache]]. They have greenish skin and dark pink plumage.

'''Hammerfall''' was formerly one of the largest of the [[Alliance]] internment camps.  It was attacked and destroyed by [[Thrall]] and the [[Horde]] in order to free the [[Orcs]] held captive there.  Shortly after the end of the [[Third War]], the Horde re-occupied the ruins of Hammerfall to use as a forward base in the [[Arathi Highlands]]. The city is so named in honor to [[Orgrim Doomhammer]], who was killed by a lance strike to the back during the camp's liberation.

[[image:Harvest_Golem.jpg|thumb|A Harvest Golem]]
The terrifying '''Harvest Watcher''' or '''Harvest Golem'''s are mechanical constructs programmed to hunt down and terminate the [[Human]] inhabitants of [[Westfall]]. Though their origin is uncertain, some believe that only the wily [[Goblin]]s could have created these mechanical monstrosities. Others speculate that the Goblins built them in order of the [[Defias Brotherhood]] to scare off the local inhabitants of Westfall so that they could run their smuggling operations with greater impunity. Whatever the case may be, the Harvest Golems have done their jobs well - eliciting terror in anyone foolish enough to roam the fallow fields of Westfall alone. They resemble giant moving scarecrows with scythe-like claws instead of hands.

[[image:Gyth.jpg|thumb|Gyth the Chromatic Dragon and Rend Blackhand]]
A large Chromatic dragon who serves as [[Rend Blackhand]]'s personal mount.
[[Rend Blackhand]] and [[Nefarian]] tested their newly created [[Chromatic Dragonflight]] against a group of heroes entering [[Blackrock Spire]], sending wave after wave of the creatures through a gated area. As they were beginning to get worn down [[Vaelan]] appeared before them, casting a massive healing spell on our entire group before teleporting off again. As still more Dragonkin attacked, Vaelan appeared once again, encouraging them to continue the fight and healing their group with his powerful magic.

Finally, Rend himself joined the fray, astride a huge chromatic drake called Gyth. Together, the two were fearsome, the drake utilizing every type of dragon breath against them while it’s rider swung his massive blade at whoever was near.

Vaelan came to our aid again, but this time in their true form; as [[Vaelastraz]] the Red. The red dragon dwarfed Gyth and Rend, and set upon them with incredible might and fury, their fiery breath forcing Rend to dismount and fight the heroes on foot. Nefarian, furious, threatened the red dragon and finally cast a spell to teleport them out of his lair. The heroes realized later that even the form of Vaelastranz they had seen here was not his real body, but rather just a projection.

With Vaelastranz gone, the heroes were alone against Rend and Gyth, but they were separated now. Gyth was confused without its master to guide it, and the group finished the beast off first, and then turned their attention to Rend. Even with so many of them, Rend was a formidable foe, using all the abilities of a seasoned blademaster to cut away at our ranks. Nevertheless, they eventually cut the warrior down, realizing too late that Nefarian had escaped in the chaos.

<The Sun had finally set on the blue lands of Moonwhisper Coast. With nightfall, its usual shepherd did not gaze upon the land. The Moon was nowhere to be seen. And yet, that was not the sole surprise, for even the youngest of the siblings, the Blue Child, was also missing. An ill sign for the children of the Earth. A superstitious folk, the Tauren believed this to be an omen of immediate chaos. Ruckus could be heard from Moonhoof Village. The celestials were missing, and so was the Elder Chieftain. Beyond their desperation, the old chieftain slowly tapped his mighty hooves on the blue grass, leaving crescent moons in the mud with each step. He approached the dreaded Grove in solemn silence.>
----
<He carried no torch, no weapon. His white fur, pale as freshly fallen snow, glimmered faintly beneath the stars. The only garment upon him was a simple kilt. His brown mane shimmered gold beneath the night as orbs of light encircled his rugged frame. Fireflies eagerly danced about him, guiding his movements through the darkness. As he pressed deeper into the Grove, he felt the gaze of the trees heavy upon the back of his neck. He was being watched. The branches stretched toward him with disdain, with unease even, yet they shrank back at once when they felt the heat of the living flame within him.>
----
<With a huff and a puff, the old Tauren finally halted. “You drink alone tonight,” he muttered, his gaze fixed upon the figure seated at a rough-hewn wooden table, sipping from a cup. Moths drifted toward him, abandoning the other Tauren’s shadow to seek the light of his fireflies. He smiled faintly, exhaling through his nose with a sound like a scoff. “You walk my Grove as though you own it, elder brother,” came a voice from behind the empty cup. A pale hand reached for the pitcher, seeking a refill.>
----
<“You still call me brother. Odd,” the old chieftain said. “Yet here you are, far from your duties, forsaking that which gave you life. You parade yourself amidst the children of chaos and bend the children of the Earth to that chaos as well.” His frown deepened, arms folding across his chest. He looked every bit the elder sibling there to discipline the younger. “Is it so strange? You came here to scold me, playing the role of my elder brother. I may as well grant you the satisfaction. You know well how I love theatrics.”>
----
<This Tauren’s fur was pale as well, but it bore the pallor of death rather than the pallor of snow. His eyes glimmered the same blue as the younger Moon. Despite his mockery, there was amusement in his gaze. “Enough quarreling, elder. Join me for a glass.” He raised his cup. “Mm. Have your servants abandoned you to your own drunken ruin?” Moonhoof asked as he approached. “I dismissed them. They could not bear the sight of your holiness.” “Enough games, brother. You know why I am here.” The elder sat beside him.>
----
<Mothshroud sighed heavily. “And what, pray tell, would that be?” Moonhoof’s jaw tightened. “Let us begin with the fact that you are possessing that poor soul’s body.” “As if you are any better. What should your actions be named, then? A blessing? A gift bestowed by the mighty, the shining…” “Enough. This one prayed for it.” Moonhoof’s brow furrowed. “So did this one,” Mothshroud said, arching a brow. “Which is precisely the problem, sibling. Why give solace to these chaotic souls? You walk among them as though they were your own. They wish for nothing but ruin. You even took in the wretched satyr. They… they are part of the reason she—” He faltered, his voice breaking.>
----
<“You cannot lay that blame at my feet. Her actions were hers alone.” “But you were meant to bring hope!” Moonhoof rose sharply, his hands clasping the back of his head in anguish. “And I still do, even among your chosen,” Mothshroud said, sipping his cup. “But I was born of pain. You know that whatever you both tried to weave could not last. I do not command them. They will follow their own will. Unlike our sibling, who basks in the adoration of the Night’s children, I walk openly among mine. We are all seen here.” “You fool. Is it jealousy that drives you?”>
----
<“Must you think so little of me, elder brother? No, I am not jealous. She may keep her pets. I have my own followers, and I will grant them precisely what they desire: hope or despair, order or chaos. And if you have come to stop me, may the stronger will prevail.” He drained his glass. “Now leave my Grove and never return. We were never meant to meet upon these lands.” “You are making a grave mistake, sibling. The Earth will mourn your choice, and I will not stand idle. My followers will have my blessings, and when they rise to trample yours, remember: this was your doing.” Moonhoof began to stamp the earth once more, leaving a crescent moon mark with each step.>
----
<“Always the self-appointed justiciar,” Mothshroud hissed, shattering the cup in his hand. “So be it. War it is.” As Mothshroud turned away, he stalked the Grove, leaving strange marks behind him. Before vanishing into the dark, he cast his gaze skyward and saw that the Moon had returned. Yet as its light bathed the land, another presence emerged beside it: the Blue Child, restored, but changed. Cold and distant, he drifted away from his elder, as though seeking to escape.>
----
<What this foretold for the children of the Earth, for Moonwhisper Coast, none could say. But the omens were dire, for kin now stood upon paths that would cross beneath the silent gaze of the Earthmother, and the blue grass would soon drink the blood of those they once held dear.>
}}
